A1.justification: Both PDFs describe KnowBias with the same authors, method and core experiments. The complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A-D are readable and support reliable matching despite the revised title and expanded appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original debiasing, reasoning, transfer, ablation and sensitivity results on Llama and Qwen models in Section 3 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds numerical evaluations on Gemma-3-4B, HolisticBias and Difference Awareness, plus a fairness-utility analysis.

M1.justification: Section 2 and Algorithm 1 retain the same bias-knowledge questions, integrated-gradient neuron attribution, attribution/frequency thresholds, union across demographic neuron sets and multiplicative inference-time enhancement. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: V2 Table 16 adds HolisticBias evaluations and Difference Awareness (N1-BBQ), extending coverage to additional bias descriptors and difference/context-awareness tasks beyond the original bias and reasoning benchmarks. HolisticBias results still cover gender, race and religion; no additional demographic axis is reported.

E2.justification: FairSteer, LFTF, ReGiFT, PEFT, BiasEdit, SD and CRISPR remain in the corresponding original comparisons. The added evaluations reuse BiasEdit or FairSteer; no baseline algorithm is introduced or removed from a retained experiment.

E3.justification: V2 adds a Gemma-3-4B evaluation configuration, Mann-Whitney U and DiffAware/CtxtAware metrics for the additional benchmarks, and a joint fairness-utility sweep of KnowBias enhancement and FairSteer regularization. Existing evaluation settings remain unchanged. Table 7's dataset counts are newly disclosed, not demonstrated sample-size revisions.

E4.justification: New Figure 4 examines how hyperparameter choices jointly affect fairness and utility for KnowBias and FairSteer. The existing question-type, aggregation, random-neuron and dimension-specific ablations remain unchanged, as do the original four sensitivity plots, now Figure 5.

E5.justification: V1 reports averages over at least ten runs without confidence intervals. V2 Tables 8-13 add 95% confidence intervals throughout the original BBQ and general-capability comparisons, with intervals also accompanying new evaluations. V2 explains their omission for deterministic CrowS-Pairs and StereoSet scores. No increase in run counts is stated.

E6.justification: Original scores in Tables 2-5, neuron counts and ablation tables are unchanged. V2 adds Gemma results, HolisticBias/N1-BBQ results and fairness-utility sweep points. For example, new Table 16 reports N1-CtxtAware of 0.4743 for KnowBias versus 0.2315 for the base model; Table 15 reports Gemma COPA accuracy of 0.6809 versus 0.6182. These evaluations were absent from v1.

T1.justification: The MLP background, integrated-gradient attribution equations, neuron-set union and activation-scaling mathematics are unchanged. No theorem, proof, formal assumption or mathematical derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims of strong debiasing, preserved utility, generalization, data efficiency and inference-time operation without retraining. The appendix additions provide supporting evidence without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix D.5 interprets the additional evaluations as supporting generalization beyond the primary benchmarks. Figure 4 specifically qualifies its tradeoff comparison as restricted to FairSteer because of limited rebuttal time. Existing mechanism explanations and the Impact Statement's substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix D.1 and Table 7 disclose evaluation counts by benchmark and demographic dimension, such as 2,836 gender, 3,440 race and 600 religion examples for BBQ-a. Core hyperparameters, hardware, runtime information and code/data access statements remain unchanged; Gemma-specific settings are not comparably detailed.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations for HolisticBias, Difference Awareness, Gemma 3 and DUET, and removes Yang et al.'s general LLM survey. Appendix A's positioning is otherwise unchanged. Updates to the existing Pan references concern publication information rather than additional research.

P1.justification: V2 changes the title to 'Knowing Bias, Doing Better', adds an offensive-content warning and acknowledgements, and inserts brief appendix dataset/results passages. Cross-references and publication text are updated, while the main narrative and most prose remain substantially identical.

P2.justification: The appendix presentation expands substantially with a dataset-size table, separate confidence-interval tables, additional evaluation tables and a new fairness-utility plot. Existing Tables 7-9 become Tables 17-19, and the original Figure 4 becomes Figure 5 without changing their content. Figure 3 is relocated within page 7.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the empirical evidence more assessable through confidence intervals and dataset counts, while the additional benchmarks, Gemma evaluation and fairness-utility sweep strengthen support for generalization and utility preservation. The gains are limited by sparse setup details for the new evaluations, unspecified confidence-interval construction and narrow comparator coverage in the added analyses. The core method and existing findings remain unchanged.
